faqs.q: What are Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes used for?
faqs.a: Seamless carbon steel tubes to ASTM A179 for heat exchangers and condensers, A192 for high-pressure boilers and A210 for boiler and superheater tubes, with EN 10216-2, BS 3059, JIS G3461 and GB/T 3087 and 5310 equivalents. Ordered by OD and minimum wall, the wall usually given as a BWG gauge. It is listed in 40 sizes, 15.88–50.8 mm outside diameter.

faqs.q: How do I read an Indus part number for Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes, such as IH-TF-CB-CS-0159-124?
faqs.a: Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes part numbers begin with IH-TF-CB-CS and then give the outside diameter in tenths of a millimetre and the wall thickness in hundredths of a millimetre. IH-TF-CB-CS-0159-124 is 15.88 mm outside diameter by 1.24 mm wall, and IH-TF-CB-CS-0508-340 is the largest size listed. Quote the full part number, or the standard, grade, OD and wall.

faqs.q: What sizes do Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes come in?
faqs.a: Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes are listed in 40 sizes, 15.88–50.8 mm outside diameter, each with its own Indus part number, for example IH-TF-CB-CS-0159-124 and IH-TF-CB-CS-0508-340. The table includes 15.88 mm OD by 1.24 mm wall and 50.80 mm OD by 3.40 mm wall.

faqs.q: What do I need to send to order Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes to the right size and grade?
faqs.a: For Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes, quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

faqs.q: How are Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes hydrostatically tested?
faqs.a: For Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes, hydrostatic test pressure: P = 32000·t/D psi (220.6·t/D MPa), capped by A450 Table 7 (highest cap 4500 psi / 31 MPa).

faqs.q: What tests and certificates come with Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes?
faqs.a: For Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes, testing follows the governing standard: A179: flattening, flaring, flange, hardness and hydrostatic tests; EN 10216-2: tensile, flattening or ring tests, leak tightness, NDT at TC2. GB/T 3087: hydro at P = 2SR/D with R = 60% of ReL, or eddy current/MFL/UT instead; Hydrostatic per A450 at P = 32000 t/D psi, or NDT at the maker's option. Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection by arrangement. Say on the enquiry which tests and inspection your project needs.

faqs.q: Which materials and grades are Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes available in?
faqs.a: Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes are available in these grades: A179; A192; A210 A-1/C; P235GH; P265GH; St35.8; St45.8; GB/T 3087 10/20.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes?
faqs.a: Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes are made to ASTM A179 / ASME SA-179, ASTM A192 / SA-192, ASTM A210 / SA-210, ASTM A450, ASTM A1016, EN 10216-2, DIN 17175 (superseded by EN 10216-2), GB/T 3087-2008, BS 3059-1/-2, JIS G3461. Tell us the standard and grade on your enquiry; equivalent grades in other standards are indicative and are checked against each tender.

faqs.q: What do Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes connect to or fit with?
faqs.a: For Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes, tubes are rolled or welded into tube sheets or headers and carried on baffles or supports, so the outside diameter and wall must match the tube sheet drilling. Related ranges are the [Precision & Mechanical Tubes](/c/precision-mechanical-tubes) and [Alloy Steel Boiler & Superheater Tubes](/c/alloy-steel-boiler-superheater-tubes) shelves.

faqs.q: How should Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes be inspected on receipt and stored?
faqs.a: Check Carbon Steel Boiler and Heat Exchanger Tubes on receipt against the order: outside diameter, wall, length, marking and the certificate heat numbers, and keep the ends capped until installation. Handle and store the material so the surface is not scratched or dented. The [Reading a mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1](/blog/en-10204-3-1-mill-test-certificate) explains how to read the certificate.
